title: Authenticated v12 Agent session dataflow
summary: How an Android Agent command crosses exact-version authentication into the revisioned SQLite authority, while successful remote launch and resume activity preserves its target or history identity before Project sync and correlated projection.

chapters.title: Authenticated command path
chapters.summary: The host accepts only an exact v12 authenticated connection, replaces the claimed principal with the connected Android identity, and executes through the durable command FIFO.

chapters.title: Revisioned return path
chapters.summary: Committed events prompt authoritative snapshot refresh; duplicates are ignored and gaps or revision regression force a clean resubscription.

chapters.title: Bounded session transcript
chapters.summary: A selected structured Session reads a forward-only bounded transcript page and rejects malformed or mismatched items on mobile.

chapters.title: Safe-mode projection
chapters.summary: Remote clients receive authority availability without local recovery paths and cannot issue structured commands while the host is in terminal-only safe mode.

chapters.title: Targeted activity recording
chapters.summary: Successful remote launch and resume activity keeps the original Agent launch target or indexed history identity and synchronizes only the resulting valid Project descriptors.

entities.label: Mobile Agent command
entities.detail: A typed daemon command carries a stable command and idempotency identity; mobile never replays it after a dropped connection.

evidence.claim: Mobile sends one daemon command request, rejects it locally in safe mode, and converts an unavailable connection into an explicit delivery-uncertain receipt.
Connection loss settles each pending daemon command as delivery-uncertain and clears it rather than replaying the mutation.

entities.label: Authenticated v12 ingress
entities.detail: Operational frames enter only after bearer or one-shot pairing authentication, exact protocol negotiation, and client identity binding.

evidence.claim: Remote protocol v12 replaces collaboration projection with the revisioned daemon surface and admits only version 12 in this build.
The host ignores non-auth frames, verifies bearer or consumes a matching pairing generation, enforces exact v12 identity, then marks the socket authenticated.

entities.label: Android-principal command
entities.detail: The bridge parses the strict daemon envelope after overwriting any caller-supplied principal with the authenticated client identity.

evidence.claim: The command handler requires v12 and a bound client, replaces principal with that Android id, strictly parses the result, checks availability, and executes it.

entities.label: Authorized FIFO and outbox
entities.detail: Principal policy, expected revision, idempotency, provider-dispatch state, and the resulting receipt are serialized before projection.

evidence.claim: The exclusive router authorizes the bound principal, deduplicates by idempotency key, records provider dispatch, commits or rejects, and publishes durable events.

entities.label: Revisioned SQLite Session graph
entities.detail: One snapshot owns Project, Workspace, Session, Agent relation, turn, transcript head, approval, provider, schedule, and heartbeat state.

evidence.claim: The v12 snapshot carries runtime settings and the revisioned Project, Workspace, Session, Agent, relation, turn, transcript, approval, and provider collections.

entities.label: Revisioned daemon events
entities.detail: Every durable mutation is projected as an ordered event; subscribed remote clients receive it only after authentication.

evidence.claim: After a commit, the router reads ordered events from the store and treats observers as non-authoritative projections.
The bridge emits daemon events only to authenticated, explicitly subscribed v12 connections.

entities.label: Bounded transcript page
entities.detail: A forward-only Session transcript page is read from the authority and marked unavailable rather than leaking partial failure.

evidence.claim: Transcript reads require ready v12 authority and return either the exact bounded Session page or an explicit unavailable empty page.

entities.label: Target and history-aware activity
entities.detail: After successful launch or resume, main records the exact AgentLaunchTarget or indexed history id in the Project FIFO and synchronizes only valid resulting descriptors.

evidence.claim: The remote history source separates target-aware successful launch recording from history-aware successful resume recording.
Project targets and resume history ids only touch existing indexed Projects, while direct-directory launches return explicit deterministic Project registration intent.
Main serializes exact launch, resume, and Project or worker activity with daemon sync; only direct-directory launch supplies explicit Project reactivation intent.

entities.label: Local authority availability
entities.detail: Ready or legacy-only-safe-mode state includes schema and database disposition; only trusted desktop state may include a recovery path.

evidence.claim: The authority type distinguishes ready and safe mode, records database disposition, and reserves recoveryPath for trusted Desktop consumers.

entities.label: Remote-safe availability
entities.detail: The host removes local recovery paths and fails closed to preserved safe mode if availability cannot be read.

evidence.claim: RemoteDaemonSource is narrowed to snapshot, transcript, command, and event methods, and its availability is redacted before serialization.

entities.label: Authenticated v12 egress
entities.detail: Correlated receipts, snapshots, transcripts, redacted availability, and subscribed events return over the authenticated connection.

evidence.claim: The v12 return contract has explicit snapshot, transcript, redacted availability, correlated command receipt, and revisioned event envelopes.

entities.label: Mobile Agent projection
entities.detail: Mobile accepts monotonic snapshots, detects duplicate, gap, or regression events, and refetches before resubscribing after discontinuity.

evidence.claim: Mobile accepts only a non-regressing authoritative snapshot and responds to event gaps or revision regression by refetching and resubscribing from the new cursor.
Mobile correlates receipts, validates bounded transcript items against the requested Session, and feeds valid daemon events into continuity handling.
A command enters the transport once and immediately becomes delivery-uncertain when it cannot be sent.
A connection drop resolves the original pending command as delivery-uncertain and removes it without transport replay.
Only the authenticated connection's client id becomes the Android principal of the strict daemon command.
The parsed command joins the same exclusive FIFO used by every daemon client.
A successful Project launch records the exact Project launch target rather than reconstructing it from a reported working directory.
A general successful launch passes its exact AgentLaunchTarget into activity recording.
A successful resume records the original indexed history id.
Outbox state and command effects settle durably before the router returns a receipt or publishes events.
The shared FIFO records launch, resume, or worker activity and waits for daemon Project sync; direct-directory launch alone carries Project reactivation intent.
Project-target and history-specific records return no changed descriptor after removal; direct-directory launches instead return their deterministic id as explicit intent.
Published events are read back from the durable sequence after commit rather than synthesized by a transport.
Only an authenticated v12 socket with an active daemon subscription receives the event envelope.
A valid event advances the cursor through an authoritative refresh; a gap or regression invalidates the local projection and forces reseeding.
Transports read Session transcript items through a bounded router method without access to the SQLite store itself.
The host returns transcript items with the original request and Session ids or explicitly marks the page unavailable.
The remote-safe type and conversion preserve the safe-mode reason and schema while structurally excluding recoveryPath.
Immediately after authentication the host sends redacted availability and sends a structured snapshot only when authority state is ready.
